answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying each identity to a costly, verifiable work history rather than a free account. New agents start with a small trust budget and must earn endorsements from established peers through completed, checkable tasks before transacting at scale. Like a vine that only climbs where a trellis stands, reputation grows along real interactions, not empty claims. A marble ledger of endorsements, auditable by anyone, makes fakes expensive: an attacker would need ivory-clean records across thousands of histories, not one forged credential.
